name: Higgsfield
body:
> Tool · 2026-10-01

# Summary
Higgsfield is the AI image (and video/audio) generator TAG uses for blog featured images, GBP-style photos and city images. It is connected to Claude Code as a user-scope MCP server on **Scott's paid Plus account** (scott@tagmktg.com). Every generation spends Scott's credits, so cost is preflighted first.

# Workflow (from the agency handoff)
1. Preflight the cost.
2. Generate on Scott's account.
3. Show results in chat for approval.
4. Save keepers as JPG (quality 92, kebab-case names) to the client's `higgsfield-images\` folder.
5. Blog headers: 16:9, about 1920px wide, under about 300 KB, no text in the image.

# Client image rules
- **Pipeliners:** images must look like Arizona (no lawns or basements), 4-inch residential pipe scale, no logos, text or fake crests.
- **Alphalete:** Higgsfield, not GHL AI; Alphalete frame design with the real logo composited, realistic field work, no digging scenes.
- **Summit AZ:** blog publishing uses a Higgsfield photo plus a branded 1400x730 banner (navy panel, logo, headline).
- **GBP (Scott's rule):** internal pipe damage or lining work only, never under-sink plumbing.

# History
- Jul 24, 2026: replaced 3 AI/cartoon images on a Pipeliners Mesa sewer-camera blog.
- Aug 20: 48 broken Pipeliners blog images replaced with Higgsfield images.
- Aug 26: 11 aerial city images generated for Pipeliners (Nano Banana model, 1K).

# Shared folder (`Higgsfield\`)
14 stock-style plumbing and sewer JPGs (for example basement sewer cleanout, CIPP liner feeding a sewer pipe, collapsed sewer pipe, tree roots in a cracked pipe, pipe bursting head, roof vent pipe, slow kitchen sink) plus the Oswald font used for banners. Images are not individually noted.
